style.notes: WEB-MWB keeps the WEB’s own modern wording (you, your, don’t, will). Name insertions add only the name and punctuation; KJV forms are never introduced.

rules.sourceText: My son, listen to your father’s instruction, and don’t forsake your mother’s teaching;
grammaticalConditions: The name follows the existing vocative "My son" and is set off by commas.
"My son" and all WEB wording are kept exactly as written.
riskReasons: Refers to the reader’s own father and mother.
rules.reviewQuestion: The WEB reads “My son, listen to your father’s instruction, and don’t forsake your mother’s teaching;” With the reader’s name added, "your father’s instruction" and "your mother’s teaching" speak of the reader’s own parents. Is personal address pastorally appropriate here, including for readers whose parents did not teach them in faith?

rules.reviewQuestion: Verse 1 opens a conditional promise fulfilled in verse 5 (“then you will understand the fear of the LORD, and find the knowledge of God.”). Is the name appropriate in the condition itself, and should verse 1 only be shown personalised together with verses 2-5?

rules.sourceText: my son, don’t walk on the path with them. Keep your foot from their path,
grammaticalConditions: In the WEB this verse begins with a lower-case "my son," continuing the warning begun in verse 10. The name follows that vocative, set off by commas.
riskReasons: Representative paternal address in wisdom instruction.

rules.sourceText: Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart, then I can answer my tormentor.
grammaticalConditions: In the WEB the vocative is mid-sentence ("Be wise, my son, and bring joy..."). The name follows "my son," and is set off by commas.
riskReasons: Representative paternal address in wisdom instruction.

rules.sourceText: Indeed surely there is a future hope, and your hope will not be cut off.
grammaticalConditions: The name is a vocative set off by commas after "and", before "your hope".
WEB wording ("Indeed surely there is a future hope", "your hope will not be cut off") is kept unchanged.
riskReasons: The assurance in verse 18 rests on the exhortation in verse 17.
rules.reviewQuestion: Verse 18’s assurance follows verse 17 (“Don’t let your heart envy sinners, but rather fear the LORD all day long.”). Should the name appear in verse 18 when it is shown on its own (daily verse, share card), or only when verse 17 is shown with it? Is ", and, [Name], your hope" natural enough in the WEB’s modern style, or should the name come elsewhere?

rules.sourceText: Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you. Don’t be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.
grammaticalConditions: The name is a vocative after "Don’t you be afraid", before the existing comma.
riskReasons: Direct divine speech.
Addressed to Israel collectively as God’s servant.
rules.reviewQuestion: This is God’s direct speech to Israel as His servant (““But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the offspring of Abraham my friend,”). May a personal name be inserted into divine speech addressed to Israel, or should this verse stay unpersonalised in WEB-MWB?

rules.sourceText: Beloved, I pray that you may prosper in all things and be healthy, even as your soul prospers.
grammaticalConditions: The name follows the existing address "Beloved," and is set off by commas.
riskReasons: Letter addressed to a specific person, Gaius.
rules.reviewQuestion: John’s prayer is addressed to Gaius (“The elder to Gaius the beloved, whom I love in truth.”). Is it appropriate to address a prayer written for a specific person to the reader by name?
